title: Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
lead: A large-scale, ==house-to-house verification== exercise to overhaul electoral rolls — distinct from the routine annual ==Summary Revision==. The SC ==upheld SIR's constitutionality== in [[ADR v. ECI (2026)]]. Conducted in ==more than 15 states== so far, with ==approximately 5 crore names removed==.

items: ==Reversal of burden of proof== — a person on the voter list is ==presumed a citizen== ([[Lal Babu Hussein v. Electoral Registration Officer, 1995]]) unless the State proves otherwise; SIR instead required voters not on the ==2002/03 legacy rolls== to prove citizenship through specified documents.

==Discriminatory documentation burden== — pre-1987 documents and parental birth certificates disproportionately burden ==SCs, STs, minorities, migrant workers, the poor, the illiterate, and women who migrated after marriage==. Historically low birth registration compounds this: ==only ~25% of births were registered in 2007==, the birth year of those turning 18 by 2025.
==Compressed timelines close to elections== — and ==Aadhaar was initially excluded== from admissible documents.

==ECI overreach into citizenship== — critics called it a ==‘backdoor NRC’==, encroaching on the Home Ministry's constitutional domain, shifting the burden of proof onto individuals with ==no clear legal framework== and risking ==permanent suspicion==.

==Assam precedent as cautionary tale== — a past SIR led to ==‘doubtful voters’ facing Foreigners' Tribunals== of arbitrary functioning; in December 2025 a Nagaon resident was pushed into Bangladesh despite due-process concerns. Tribunal member qualifications ==weakened over time== — from mandatory retired judges in 1964 to ==any lawyer with seven years' experience== today.

==Data disputes and administrative errors== — contradictory deletion claims; ==persons declared dead found alive and vice versa==; the ECI maintained ==7.24 of 7.9 crore voters== had responded, disputing claims of mass disenfranchisement.
==Administrative strain== — increasingly exclusionary, opaque and burdensome; ==BLO deaths== reported from unrealistic deadlines; ==2002–04 legacy rolls poorly digitised==.

==Institutional design gap== — unchecked institutional power: the ECI's own appointment process (post the ==2023 Act replacing the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister==, itself challenged in [[Jaya Thakur v. UoI]]) raises independence questions.
==Post-facto judicial review== — the verdict came ==six months after the Bihar polls==, so judicial correction could not undo wrongful exclusions.

sections.title: Global Best Practices in Roll Maintenance

items: ==Continuous/automatic voter registration== (much of Europe, parts of the US) — rolls updated in real time via linkage with ==civil registration and residency databases==, avoiding disruptive periodic exercises.
==UK==: rolling annual canvass with ==Individual Electoral Registration==, supplemented by ==data-matching against government records== rather than blanket re-verification.
==Canada==: a ==National Register of Electors== updated continuously via tax, immigration and vital statistics linkages — voters ==never re-prove eligibility==.
==Germany==: registration near-automatic via mandatory municipal residence registration (==Meldewesen==).

==International principle== — ==UN HRC General Comment 25==: any restriction on the right to vote must rest on ==objective, reasonable criteria== with adequate safeguards, ==including a fair hearing before removal==.

blocks.text: ==Common thread==: mature democracies ==minimise burden-shifting onto citizens== by relying on ==inter-agency data integration== rather than repeated door-to-door documentary re-verification.

items: ==Institutionalise continuous roll updation== via privacy-safeguarded linkage to birth/death registers
==Restore and codify the Lal Babu Hussein presumption== — exclusion requires ==individualised inquiry and a reasoned, appealable order==, not a blanket document mandate
==Decouple SIR timing from elections== — statutory ==cooling-off periods== before scheduled polls

==Widen and simplify the documentary regime== — accept Aadhaar and widely-held IDs from the outset; ==community verification and sworn affidavits== (with penalties for false claims) for those without legacy documents
==Strengthen appellate infrastructure== — judicially trained tribunals, distinct from the criticised ==Foreigners' Tribunal model==
==Clarify institutional boundaries== — SIR confined to roll eligibility, ==never a proxy citizenship determination==; citizenship doubts routed through the Citizenship Act
==Independent, multi-partisan ECI appointments== — resolving Jaya Thakur and restoring a broad-based selection process
==Transparency by design== — real-time, searchable, ==reasoned deletion databases== as standard, not a court-ordered afterthought
==Time-bound judicial review== — expedited mechanisms so constitutional questions are resolved ==before, not after, the election==

blocks.text: Electoral integrity demands clean rolls; constitutional democracy demands inclusive rolls. The real test of SIR lies in reconciling both — because a democracy is weakened as much by a fraudulent vote as by the silencing of a genuine one.
